The current camel toolbox services define an activemq bean directly in the blueprint configuration. If Fedora begins to support multiple messaging systems  and protocols, it would be much better to externalize that as a generic OSGi "queuing" service. This has several advantages: first, it means that all message broker configuration can be centralized, and second, it means that the JMS service can be dynamically swapped out for AMQP, Kafka, etc, etc.

Actually, this applies to the fcrepo bean, too. By wrapping that in an OSGi service, there would be only a single component to configure: none of this redundant configuration would be necessary.

This will result in a change in how users deploy and run the camel toolkit, so when this is merged, it will involve a minor version bump (4.6.0).
This would supersede FCREPO-2013 Closed , but I would like to see FCREPO-2013 Closed go into a fcrepo-camel-toolbox/4.5.2 release before the restructuring of FCREPO-2017 Closed is merged.
An implementation is ready, but submitting a PR is now on hold until FCREPO-2013 Closed is merged and a fcrepo-camel-toolbox/4.5.2 release is cut.

Is there a way to manage the activemq broker?

For some reason, I cannot see the activemq plugin in hawtio. The issue that I need to solve is related to managing reindexing queues. Also, if I add activemq-broker in karaf and run activemq:list I see nothing.

My specific problem with reindexing is that I have long running tasks that I cannot seem to purge, and these are attempting to index deleted objects in the repository. Even if I change the configuration to retry attempts 1, the reindexer still continues with the old queued message. These errors begin with "Failed delivery for (MessageId: ID:". I attach a stack trace of the error for reference. stacktrace

One other minor problem, there seems to be something missing in the toolbox build. If I follow this command sequence:

karaf@root()> feature:repo-add mvn:org.fcrepo.camel/toolbox-features/LATEST/xml/features
Adding feature url mvn:org.fcrepo.camel/toolbox-features/LATEST/xml/features
karaf@root()> feature:install fcrepo-service-activemq
karaf@root()> feature:install fcrepo-reindexing
karaf@root()> feature:install fcrepo-serialization
karaf@root()> feature:install fcrepo-indexing-triplestore
karaf@root()> Exception in thread "ActiveMQ InactivityMonitor WriteCheckTimer" java.lang.NoClassDefFoundError: org/apache/activemq/transport/AbstractInactivityMonitor$4
at org.apache.activemq.transport.AbstractInactivityMonitor.writeCheck(AbstractInactivityMonitor.java:188)
at org.apache.activemq.transport.AbstractInactivityMonitor$3.run(AbstractInactivityMonitor.java:152)
at org.apache.activemq.thread.SchedulerTimerTask.run(SchedulerTimerTask.java:33)
at java.util.TimerThread.mainLoop(Timer.java:555)
at java.util.TimerThread.run(Timer.java:505)
Caused by: java.lang.ClassNotFoundException: Unable to load class 'org.apache.activemq.transport.AbstractInactivityMonitor$4' because the bundle wiring for org.apache.activemq.activemq-osgi is no longer valid.

If you're using a local broker for the reindexing queue (a good idea), you can purge that with the purge command. Documentation is here: http://activemq.apache.org/osgi-integration.html

For details on the command, use activemq:purge --help

If you're using Fedora's embedded broker for the queue, then it may be best to just write something to read off all the messages, as there is no good mechanism for managing that broker. In that case, you should be able to easily adapt something like this (python): https://www.ats.amherst.edu/~acoburn/listener.py
